definitions.type: ℕ → real finite dimensional inner product spaces
definitions.definition: Ambient(m)=EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m), the space of m real coordinates with norm ‖x‖₂=(Σ_{j<m}|x_j|²)^(1/2). The sum is zero when m=0. Distances are norms of differences.

definitions.type: extended diameter of a subset of any pseudo extended metric space
definitions.definition: For a pseudo extended metric space Z and B⊆Z, ediam(B)=sup{edist(x,y):x∈B,y∈B} in [0,∞], with supremum of the empty set zero. For finite ediam, diam(B)=(ediam B).toReal and ediam B=ofReal(diam B). In metric spaces edist is ofReal of the ordinary distance.
ofReal(v) is max(v,0) embedded in the extended nonnegative reals. The notation z.toReal for z∈[0,∞] is its real value when finite, and zero for z=∞.

definitions.type: real exponent × extended scale × subset of an extended metric space → [0,∞]
definitions.definition: For an extended metric space Z, exponent u∈ℝ, scale h∈[0,∞], and B⊆Z, Content(u,h,B)=inf_{U:ℕ→Set Z; B⊆⋃_i U_i; ∀i ediam(U_i)≤h} Σ_i sup_{(_ : U_i nonempty)} (ediam U_i)^u. Infima, suprema and sums are in [0,∞]; an infimum over no covers is ∞. This is exactly the Content in basis-registry.json /lean_header. Countable covers may be padded by empty sets.

definitions.type: real exponent × real scale × subset → [0,∞]
definitions.definition: C_u(h,B), also written C_u(h,B), means Content(u,ofReal h,B) for real scale h. We use it only at h>0.

binders.type: subset of an extended metric space

definitions.type: real exponent × subset of a Borel extended metric space → [0,∞]
definitions.definition: H^u(B)=μH[u](B) denotes Mathlib's unnormalized Hausdorff measure, the metric measure mkMetric for the gauge r↦r^u. Here mkMetric is the Borel metric-measure construction: at each scale take the countable-cover outer content for the gauge, with the empty-set gauge cost forced to zero, and take its small-scale supremum. The precise evaluation identity used for this native measure is the explicit source M001. No spherical or dimensional normalization factor is used.

binders.type: subset of a Borel extended metric space

definitions.type: subset of an extended metric space → [0,∞]
definitions.definition: For B in an extended metric space, equipped with its Borel measurable structure when computing H, dimH(B)=sup{d∈[0,∞): H^d(B)=∞}, the supremum taken in [0,∞] and with sup ∅=0. This is native Mathlib dimH. For positive exponents its critical-exponent directions are the sources M002–M005. We use no zero-exponent measure assertion.

binders.type: subset of an extended metric space

definitions.type: subset of ℝ
definitions.definition: I=[0,1]={t∈ℝ:0≤t≤1}. This is unitInterval in the basis header.

definitions.type: metric space → metric spaces
definitions.definition: For a metric space Z, MaxProd(Z)=Z×ℝ with distance d_max((x,t),(y,u))=max(d_Z(x,y),|t−u|). For B⊆Z, B×I always denotes a subset of MaxProd(Z) in intermediate lemmas. All metric spaces in integration or Hausdorff-measure statements carry their Borel sigma algebra.

definitions.type: for m∈ℕ, MaxProd(Ambient m) → Ambient(m+1)
definitions.definition: appendCoord(m)(x,t) is the vector whose first m coordinates are those of x and whose last coordinate is t. In the exact basis header it is WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.lastCases t (fun j => x j)). Its target always carries the Euclidean norm; its source here carries the maximum metric. It is a total coordinate construction, including m=0. Under the problem's identification ℝ^n×ℝ=ℝ^(n+1), the Euclidean set E×[0,1] is appendCoord(n) '' (E×I).

definitions.type: measure on the Borel sets of ℝ
definitions.definition: volume is Lebesgue measure on ℝ, with its usual Borel measurable structure (and its extension as an outer measure on arbitrary sets). Thus measure monotonicity applies to all subsets; no measurability of a covering set is implicit.

definitions.type: subset × constant → functions
definitions.definition: For a set B⊆Z and a scalar c∈[0,∞], c1_B denotes the function equal to c on B and zero off B, that is B.indicator(fun _ => c). This is meaningful for c=∞ as well, with no subtraction of infinities.

definitions.type: measure × nonnegative extended function → [0,∞]
definitions.definition: For a measurable space Z, measure μ and f:Z→[0,∞], ∫⁻ f dμ (the lower Lebesgue integral, lintegral) is the supremum of ∫g dμ over measurable nonnegative simple functions g≤f; a simple function integral is its finite sum of values times the measures of the corresponding disjoint level sets. All integrals in the slicing proof are lower integrals; integrability is never required.

binders.type: nonnegative measurable simple function on Z

definitions.type: nonnegative real × map of pseudo extended metric spaces → propositions
definitions.definition: LipschitzWith(K,f) means ∀x,y, edist(f x,f y)≤K·edist(x,y), where K is a finite nonnegative real embedded into [0,∞]. On metric spaces this is the usual distance inequality.

binders.type: map between pseudo extended metric spaces

definitions.type: nonnegative real × map of extended metric spaces → propositions
definitions.definition: AntilipschitzWith(L,f) means ∀x,y, edist(x,y)≤L·edist(f x,f y), with finite L≥0. On metric spaces this is the corresponding ordinary distance inequality.

definitions.type: ordered field or real vector space × endpoints → subsets
definitions.definition: segment(k,x,y)={a•x+b•y: a,b∈k, a≥0,b≥0,a+b=1}, in a vector space over an ordered scalar field k; over ℝ this is the usual closed line segment.

definitions.type: field × vector space → ℕ
definitions.definition: finrank(k,Z) is the dimension as a natural number of a finite-dimensional k-vector space Z (and is zero by the native total convention if the vector-space rank is infinite). In this proof its arguments are finite dimensional.

definitions.type: real or extended nonnegative base × real exponent → corresponding scalars
definitions.definition: The notation v^u uses the standard real power; on positive real v it is exp(u log v), with 0^u=0 for u>0 and 0^0=1. For extended nonnegative bases it is the usual extension: at u>0, ∞^u=∞ and 0^u=0; at u=0 the value is 1; at u<0, 0^u=∞ and ∞^u=0. Only nonnegative real bases and positive exponents occur in the covering calculations. The native real function at negative v is defined using |v|, as in Real.rpow.

argument.text: Ambient n is the n-coordinate real inner product space, hence a finite-dimensional real normed vector space: its n coordinate vectors span and are independent, also for the empty coordinate family at n=0. Nonnegativity is part of the [0,∞] codomain of dimH. M010 applied to E in the same space gives dimH E≠∞. No compactness or nonemptiness is used.

locals.declaration: Fix an arbitrary metric space X with its Borel sigma algebra.
Choose a cover U as in the earlier existence statement F002.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary X,A,s, and assume L1: s>0. For an empty cover member, ediam ∅=0 and 0^s=0, so its guarded cost in Content is zero, exactly the raw diameter-power cost. For a nonempty member the supremum over its nonemptiness witnesses is that same power. Thus C_s is the stated raw countable-cover infimum. If 0<δ₁≤δ₂, each δ₁-cover is a δ₂-cover; taking infima gives C_s(δ₂,A)≤C_s(δ₁,A). Apply M001 at X,A,s. Its positive extended-scale supremum equals the positive finite real-scale supremum: every finite positive real scale is an allowed extended scale, while any h∈(0,∞] admits a finite real δ>0 with ofReal δ≤h (take δ=h.toReal/2 when h<∞, and δ=1 when h=∞). Scale antitonicity then bounds the content at h by the one at δ. This proves the normalization and supremum statements F001. The countable covers here are exactly those in problem.md; finite covers can be padded by empty sets.

produces.statement: For this X,A,s>0, C_s is the raw positive-exponent cover infimum, is antitone on positive scales, and H^s(A)=sup_{δ>0,δ∈ℝ} C_s(δ,A).

argument.text: Fix arbitrary real r,ε, and assume L2: H^s(A)=0, r>0 and ε>0. F001 and nonnegativity give C_s(r/2,A)=0. The defining infimum then has a cover with cost <ofReal(ε/4): if no admissible cover had cost below that positive number, the infimum would be at least that number. In particular admissible covers exist; otherwise the infimum is ∞. This proves F002.

produces.statement: There exists U:ℕ→Set X covering A, with ediam U_i≤ofReal(r/2) for every i and Σ_i (ediam U_i)^s<ofReal(ε/4).

argument.text: Choose U from F002, and define d_i=(ediam U_i).toReal and e_i=ε·2^(−i−3). Since ediam U_i≤ofReal(r/2)<∞, we have 0≤d_i≤r/2<r and ediam U_i=ofReal d_i. Therefore the original cost is Σ_i ofReal(d_i^s)<ofReal(ε/4). Each e_i is positive and Σ_i e_i=ε/4: the first m terms sum to (ε/4)(1−2^(−m)), tending to ε/4. These finite partial sums also establish the corresponding extended-nonnegative sum identity.

produces.statement: U covers A; 0≤d_i≤r/2<r, ediam U_i=ofReal d_i, Σ_i ofReal(d_i^s)<ofReal(ε/4), e_i>0 and Σ_i ofReal(e_i)=ofReal(ε/4).

argument.text: Use M020 with exponent s≥0. For each natural index i, continuity of x↦x^s at d_i and the strict gap d_i<r from F003 permit a positive η_i smaller than r−d_i and small enough that |(d_i+η_i)^s−d_i^s|<e_i. Indeed the continuity neighborhood for error e_i>0 contains an interval about d_i, and one can take half the minimum of its positive radius and r−d_i. Then d_i+η_i is in (d_i,r) and its s-power is <d_i^s+e_i. Countable choice of these individual values yields the sequence-existence statement F004; no covering sets are enlarged.

produces.statement: There exists a:ℕ→ℝ with d_i<a_i≤r and a_i^s<d_i^s+e_i for all natural i.

argument.text: Choose a from F004. By F003 and F004, 0<a_i≤r and ediam U_i=ofReal d_i≤ofReal a_i. Comparing nonnegative finite partial sums and then their suprema gives Σ_i ofReal(a_i^s)≤Σ_i ofReal(d_i^s)+Σ_i ofReal(e_i)<ofReal(ε/2)<ofReal ε. Addition of these nonnegative sums is justified by the finite partial-sum identity and taking increasing suprema; all right-hand totals here are finite. This proves the required cover and positive budgets for every r,ε under L2. Discharge L2 into the stated implication, and discharge L1 into the positive-exponent universal statement. Together with F001 this proves all clauses of N101. Empty cover members received positive numerical budgets in the same way; the proof also works in singleton and zero-dimensional spaces.

Fix a finite real scale δ.
Fix an arbitrary sequence V of subsets of MaxProd X.
Define ρ_i=(ediam V_i).toReal, including ρ_i=0 when V_i is empty.
Define Aproj_i as the projection of V_i to X.
Define Bproj_i as the projection of V_i to ℝ.
For each i define J_i=[inf Bproj_i,sup Bproj_i] if V_i is nonempty, and J_i=∅ otherwise.
Define W(t)_i=Aproj_i if t∈J_i and ∅ otherwise.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary X,A,s,δ and assume L1: s>0 and δ>0. Fix an arbitrary sequence V and assume L2: V covers A×I and ediam V_i≤ofReal δ for every i. Define ρ_i=(ediam V_i).toReal, Aproj_i=π_X(V_i), Bproj_i=π_ℝ(V_i). All ρ_i lie in [0,δ], and ediam V_i=ofReal ρ_i. The two coordinate projections are 1-Lipschitz, since each coordinate distance is bounded by their maximum, the source distance. Applying M021 to each projection therefore gives ediam Aproj_i≤ofReal ρ_i and ediam Bproj_i≤ofReal ρ_i. For empty V_i both projections and their diameters are empty and zero. This proves F001.

produces.statement: For every i, 0≤ρ_i≤δ, ediam V_i=ofReal ρ_i, ediam Aproj_i≤ofReal ρ_i, ediam Bproj_i≤ofReal ρ_i. Empty V_i have empty projections and ρ_i=0.

argument.text: Each Bproj_i is bounded in ℝ. If it is empty this is immediate. Otherwise, for any t_i∈Bproj_i, every t∈Bproj_i satisfies |t−t_i|≤ρ_i by F001 and the defining diameter bound. Thus Bproj_i⊆[t_i−ρ_i,t_i+ρ_i], a bounded interval. This proves the boundedness statement F002 without choosing any measurable projection or any uniform center.

produces.statement: Every real projection Bproj_i is bounded.

argument.text: Define J_i=[inf Bproj_i,sup Bproj_i] for nonempty V_i and J_i=∅ for empty V_i. For a nonempty index, M018 and F002 give Bproj_i⊆J_i, M017 gives ediam Bproj_i=ofReal(sup Bproj_i−inf Bproj_i), and M019 gives volume(J_i)=that same quantity≤ofReal ρ_i by F001. For empty indices inclusion and the zero volume bound are immediate. Every J_i is closed (or empty), hence Borel measurable; so is J_i∩I because I is closed. M019 at 0,1 also gives volume(I)=ofReal(1−0)=1. These are F003.

produces.statement: For every i, Bproj_i⊆J_i, J_i and J_i∩I are Borel measurable, and volume(J_i)≤ofReal ρ_i. Also I is Borel measurable and volume(I)=1; empty V_i give J_i=∅.

argument.text: Put c=C_s(δ,A) and W(t)_i=Aproj_i if t∈J_i, otherwise ∅. For each t∈I these sets cover A: for any x∈A, the cover V contains (x,t) in some V_i, hence x∈Aproj_i and t∈Bproj_i⊆J_i by F003. Each W(t)_i has extended diameter≤ofReal δ by F001, and its s-cost is at most ofReal(ρ_i^s)1_{J_i}(t), since s>0. N101's raw infimum formula yields c≤Σ_i ofReal(ρ_i^s)1_{J_i}(t). Define h=c1_I and g_i=ofReal(ρ_i^s)1_{J_i∩I}. On I the preceding inequality gives h≤Σ_i g_i; outside I both sides are zero. All g_i and h are Borel measurable: they take fixed constants on measurable sets and zero elsewhere, also when c=∞. This proves F004; we never require c to be finite.

produces.statement: h=c1_I and g_i=ofReal(ρ_i^s)1_{J_i∩I} are measurable nonnegative extended functions on ℝ, and h≤Σ_i g_i pointwise on ℝ.

argument.text:
Integrate the pointwise inequality of F004 with respect to volume on ℝ by M016. Apply M014 to the natural-indexed measurable family g, and M015 to h=c1_I and to each g_i. Using F003 and measure monotonicity gives
c=c·volume(I)=∫⁻h≤∫⁻Σ_i g_i=Σ_i∫⁻g_i
 =Σ_i ofReal(ρ_i^s) volume(J_i∩I)
 ≤Σ_i ofReal(ρ_i^s) volume(J_i)
 ≤Σ_i ofReal(ρ_i^s) ofReal ρ_i
 =Σ_i ofReal(ρ_i^(s+1))=Σ_i(ediam V_i)^(s+1).
For ρ_i>0 the last power identity is ρ_i^s·ρ_i=ρ_i^(s+1); for ρ_i=0 both s and s+1 are positive so both sides are zero. Empty indices also contribute zero. Measure monotonicity needs no additional measurability condition. Nonnegative sums are compared by finite partial sums and their suprema. These operations hold in [0,∞], with 0·∞=0 as usual; c·1=c even for c=∞. Since V was arbitrary, discharge L2 and universally quantify V. This is F005.

produces.statement: Every natural-indexed δ-cover V0 of A×I satisfies C_s(δ,A)≤Σ_i (ediam V0_i)^(s+1).

argument.text: Take the infimum of the cover costs in F005. N101 applies to exponent s+1>0 and gives C_s(δ,A)≤C_{s+1}(δ,A×I). This infimum argument is valid even if no δ-cover exists, in which case its right-hand infimum is ∞. The argument holds for every real δ>0. Take the supremum over these scales, and use N101 for both spaces and positive exponents s and s+1, to obtain H^s(A)≤H^{s+1}(A×I). Discharge L1 and universally quantify X,A,s,δ. This proves N102 with constant one, for arbitrary subsets and without compactness.

argument.text: Fix X,A,q, and assume L1: q>0 and H^q(A)=0. Fix arbitrary real δ,ε and assume L2: δ>0 and ε>0. Define r=min(1,δ)>0. N101, instantiated with s=q and this r,ε, gives existence of a pair consisting of a cover U of A and budgets a_i with 0<a_i≤r, ediam U_i≤ofReal a_i and Σ_i ofReal(a_i^q)<ofReal ε. Record this as F001 before choosing the pair.

produces.statement: There exist U:ℕ→Set X and a:ℕ→ℝ, chosen as one pair, such that U covers A, 0<a_i≤r, ediam U_i≤ofReal a_i, and Σ_i ofReal(a_i^q)<ofReal ε.

argument.text:
Choose the pair (U,a) from F001. Define N_i=ceil(1/a_i). Since 0<a_i≤r≤1, N_i≥1, 1/N_i≤a_i and N_i≤1/a_i+1≤2/a_i. Partition I by the N_i closed intervals Jpart_(i,j)=[j/N_i,(j+1)/N_i] for 0≤j<N_i. The products Ppart_(i,j)=U_i×Jpart_(i,j) cover A×I. Distances within each product are bounded by max(a_i,1/N_i)≤a_i, so its extended diameter is ≤ofReal a_i≤ofReal δ. Their index set {(i,j): i∈ℕ,0≤j<N_i} injects into ℕ×ℕ, which is enumerated by successive finite diagonals. Thus the products can be reindexed as a natural sequence, with empty padding if necessary. Reindexing preserves the sum of nonnegative costs: both are suprema of the same finite subfamily sums. Their total (q+1)-cost satisfies
Σ_i Σ_{j<N_i}(ediam Ppart_(i,j))^(q+1)
 ≤Σ_i ofReal(N_i a_i^(q+1))
 ≤Σ_i ofReal((2/a_i)a_i^(q+1))
 =2Σ_i ofReal(a_i^q)<ofReal(2ε).
All divisions are by positive a_i; real powers give a_i^(q+1)/a_i=a_i^q. This proves the countable-cover existence and cost bound F002, with absolute constant 2.

produces.statement: There exists a natural-indexed δ-cover of A×I in MaxProd X with total (q+1)-cost <ofReal(2ε).

argument.text: N101 identifies C_{q+1}(δ,A×I) with the cover-cost infimum. By F002 it is ≤ofReal(2ε) for every ε>0 at each fixed δ>0, so it is zero: any positive finite lower bound is contradicted by taking a smaller ε, and even one such finite bound excludes ∞. Discharge L2 to obtain the asserted existence for every δ,ε>0 and zero content for every δ>0. N101's finite-positive-scale supremum then yields H^{q+1}(A×I)=0. Discharge L1 and universally quantify X,A,q. This proves both N103 clauses, including the scale/tolerance statement and its constant.
Fix X,A and assume L1: A is nonempty. This says precisely that there exists a point x₀∈A, the existence recorded as F001.

produces.statement: There exists x₀∈X with x₀∈A.

argument.text: Choose x₀∈A from F001 and define f:ℝ→MaxProd X by f(t)=(x₀,t). For all real t,u, d_max(f(t),f(u))=max(d_X(x₀,x₀),|t−u|)=max(0,|t−u|)=|t−u|. Thus f is both 1-Lipschitz and 1-antilipschitz. Also f '' I⊆A×I, because x₀∈A. Record these facts as F002.

produces.statement: f is 1-Lipschitz and 1-antilipschitz from ℝ to MaxProd X, and f '' I⊆A×I.

argument.text: Apply M006 and M007 to f and I using F002; their two opposite image inequalities give dimH(f '' I)=dimH I. N005 says dimH I=1. Apply M008 in MaxProd X to the inclusion in F002, obtaining 1=dimH(f '' I)≤dimH(A×I). Discharge L1 and quantify X,A. This proves N104; the chosen point's identity is absent from the conclusion.

locals.declaration: Fix an arbitrary metric space X with its Borel sigma algebra.
For the upper-bound contradiction define qmid=D0+(T0−D0−1)/2.
For the lower-bound contradiction define smid=(max(0,T0−1)+D0)/2.

argument.text: Fix X,A and assume L1: A is nonempty and dimH A≠∞. Define D0=(dimH A).toReal and G=A×I. Since dimH A is finite and nonnegative, D0≥0 and ofReal D0=dimH A. This establishes F001 and legitimately permits approximation by real exponents.

produces.statement: D0≥0, ofReal D0=dimH A, A is nonempty, and G=A×I in MaxProd X.

argument.text: Fix an arbitrary real q and assume L2: q>D0. Then q>0 by F001. Instantiate M003 with subset A and nonnegative exponent q: ofReal q>dimH A, so H^q(A)=0. N103 with X,A,q yields H^{q+1}(G)=0. Record this exact measure conclusion as F002.

Apply M004 in MaxProd X to G and exponent q+1>0, using F002's zero measure (zero≠∞). It gives dimH G≤ofReal(q+1). Since q was arbitrary, discharge L2 into the complete universally quantified assertion F003.

produces.statement: For every real q0>D0, dimH G≤ofReal(q0+1).

argument.text: Take q0=D0+1 in F003; the resulting finite upper bound proves dimH G≠∞. Define T0=(dimH G).toReal, so T0≥0 and ofReal T0=dimH G. To prove the sharp upper bound, assume L3: T0>D0+1, and define qmid=D0+(T0−D0−1)/2. Then qmid>D0 and qmid+1<T0. F003 at qmid gives T0≤qmid+1, a contradiction. Discharge L3 by classical contradiction, obtaining T0≤D0+1. Independently, N104 applies to the nonempty A from F001 and gives dimH G≥1, hence T0≥1. These finite-dimension and bound facts are F004.

produces.statement: dimH G≠∞, T0≥1, ofReal T0=dimH G, and T0≤D0+1.

argument.text: Fix an arbitrary real s and assume L4: 0<s<D0. By F001, ofReal s<dimH A. M002 at subset A and nonnegative exponent s gives H^s(A)=∞, the exact assertion F005.

produces.statement: s>0 and H^s(A)=∞.

argument.text: Instantiate N102 with X,A,s. Since s>0, F005 and its measure inequality give ∞=H^s(A)≤H^{s+1}(A×I)=H^{s+1}(G), so H^{s+1}(G)=∞. This is F006.
Apply M005 in MaxProd X at subset G and exponent s+1, using F006. It gives ofReal(s+1)≤dimH G, hence s+1≤T0 by F004. Discharge L4 and quantify the arbitrary s to obtain F007.

produces.statement: For every real s0 with 0<s0<D0, s0+1≤T0.

argument.text: By D0≥0 from F001, the cases D0=0 and D0>0 are exhaustive. In the first branch assume L5: D0=0. F004 gives T0≥1=D0+1; close this branch and discharge L5. In the second branch assume L6: D0>0. To prove T0≥D0+1 assume L7: T0<D0+1 and define smid=(max(0,T0−1)+D0)/2. Both 0 and T0−1 are <D0, so max(0,T0−1)<smid<D0. In particular smid>0 and T0<smid+1, whereas F007 gives smid+1≤T0. This is a contradiction; discharge L7, obtaining T0≥D0+1 in this branch, and discharge L6. Case elimination therefore gives T0≥D0+1 universally. With F004's opposite bound, T0=D0+1. Since ofReal D0=dimH A and ofReal T0=dimH G, this is dimH(A×I)=dimH A+1 in [0,∞]. The finiteness clause is F004. Discharge L1 and quantify X,A; this proves N105, including the case D0=0.

locals.declaration: Fix an arbitrary source point p.
Fix another arbitrary source point p′.
Fix an arbitrary subset S of the maximum-metric product.

argument.text:
The map appendCoord(n) places the n coordinates of its first component before its real second component. Its inverse reads off these first n coordinates and the last coordinate. These coordinate operations are inverse in both orders, so the map is bijective. Fix arbitrary source points p,p′ and put a=‖p.1−p′.1‖₂≥0, b=|p.2−p′.2|≥0. Splitting the finite sum of squares into the first n terms and the last term gives
 d₂(appendCoord(n)p,appendCoord(n)p′)^2
   =Σ_{i<n}|p.1_i−p′.1_i|²+|p.2−p′.2|²=a²+b².
Since max(a,b)²≤a²+b²≤2max(a,b)², taking nonnegative square roots gives
 d_max(p,p′)≤d₂(appendCoord(n)p,appendCoord(n)p′)≤√2·d_max(p,p′).
The maximum is exactly the source distance. Quantifying p,p′, these inequalities establish √2-Lipschitz and 1-antilipschitz bounds. When n=0, the coordinate sum is empty and zero, the first component is the unique vector of Ambient 0, and the same inverse and estimates still apply. Record the full construction and bounds as F001.

produces.statement: appendCoord(n):MaxProd(Ambient n)→Ambient(n+1) is bijective, is √2-Lipschitz and 1-antilipschitz, and its distances satisfy d_max(p0,p1)≤d₂(appendCoord(n)p0,appendCoord(n)p1)≤√2·d_max(p0,p1) for all source points p0,p1. This holds including n=0.

argument.text: Fix an arbitrary subset S⊆MaxProd(Ambient n). Apply M006 with map appendCoord(n) and K=√2≥0, using F001, to obtain dimH(appendCoord(n) '' S)≤dimH S. Apply M007 with the same map and L=1, again using F001, to obtain the reverse inequality. Antisymmetry gives equality for every S. Together with F001's bijectivity and the two explicit distance bounds, this proves N106. Both constants are absolute; no norm-invariance assertion is assumed.

applications.bindings: Z=MaxProd(Ambient n), W=Ambient(n+1), K=√2 as a nonnegative real, f=appendCoord(n), subset S.
hypothesis_checks: Both the maximum-product and target Euclidean metrics are metric spaces; √2 is finite and nonnegative.
F001 proves the upper distance bound for every pair, exactly the √2-Lipschitz premise.

applications.bindings: Z=MaxProd(Ambient n), W=Ambient(n+1), L=1, f=appendCoord(n), subset S.
hypothesis_checks: The same metric spaces supply extended metrics and 1 is nonnegative.

argument.text: Return to the original natural n and E⊆Ambient n. H001 gives that E is nonempty. N004 gives dimH E≤n and dimH E≠∞, including n=0. Instantiate N105 with X=Ambient n and A=E. Its nonemptiness and finite-dimension conditions are exactly these two available facts. It yields dimH(E×I)=dimH E+1 in MaxProd(Ambient n), and finiteness of that product dimension. Now apply N106 to the subset E×I. Under the fixed coordinate identification, appendCoord(n) '' (E×I) is precisely the original E×[0,1] in Euclidean ℝ^(n+1): its first n coordinates belong to E and its last coordinate belongs to [0,1], and conversely every such vector has this preimage. N106 transfers the maximum-metric dimension to this Euclidean image. Therefore dimH(E×[0,1])=dimH E+1 with the stipulated Euclidean metric. Both sides are finite by N004 and N105, so their [0,∞] equality is the equality of finite real dimensions as well. This proves P. The original compactness H002 remains retained but is unused in this strengthened basis route.

original_context.full_target:
Here dimension means **Hausdorff dimension**. As approved by the user on
2026-10-23, assume explicitly that \(E\) is nonempty. With the convention
\(\dim_H\varnothing=0\), the printed equality would otherwise fail for
the empty set. This is a disclosed addition to the printed exercise.

Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove

\[
\dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
\]

The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary X,A,s, and assume L1: s>0. For an empty cover member, ediam ∅=0 and 0^s=0, so its guarded cost in Content is zero, exactly the raw diameter-power cost. For a nonempty member the supremum over its nonemptiness witnesses is that same power. Thus C_s is the stated raw countable-cover infimum. If 0<δ₁≤δ₂, each δ₁-cover is a δ₂-cover; taking infima gives C_s(δ₂,A)≤C_s(δ₁,A). Apply M001 at X,A,s. Its positive extended-scale supremum equals the positive finite real-scale supremum: every finite positive real scale is an allowed extended scale, while any h∈(0,∞] admits a finite real δ>0 with ofReal δ≤h (take δ=h.toReal/2 when h<∞, and δ=1 when h=∞). Scale antitonicity then bounds the content at h by the one at δ. This proves the normalization and supremum statements F001. The countable covers here are exactly those in problem.md; finite covers can be padded by empty sets.

produces.statement: For this X,A,s>0, C_s is the raw positive-exponent cover infimum, is antitone on positive scales, and H^s(A)=sup_{δ>0,δ∈ℝ} C_s(δ,A).

argument.text: Fix arbitrary real r,ε, and assume L2: H^s(A)=0, r>0 and ε>0. F001 and nonnegativity give C_s(r/2,A)=0. The defining infimum then has a cover with cost <ofReal(ε/4): if no admissible cover had cost below that positive number, the infimum would be at least that number. In particular admissible covers exist; otherwise the infimum is ∞. This proves F002.

produces.statement: There exists U:ℕ→Set X covering A, with ediam U_i≤ofReal(r/2) for every i and Σ_i (ediam U_i)^s<ofReal(ε/4).

argument.text: Choose U from F002, and define d_i=(ediam U_i).toReal and e_i=ε·2^(−i−3). Since ediam U_i≤ofReal(r/2)<∞, we have 0≤d_i≤r/2<r and ediam U_i=ofReal d_i. Therefore the original cost is Σ_i ofReal(d_i^s)<ofReal(ε/4). Each e_i is positive and Σ_i e_i=ε/4: the first m terms sum to (ε/4)(1−2^(−m)), tending to ε/4. These finite partial sums also establish the corresponding extended-nonnegative sum identity.

produces.statement: U covers A; 0≤d_i≤r/2<r, ediam U_i=ofReal d_i, Σ_i ofReal(d_i^s)<ofReal(ε/4), e_i>0 and Σ_i ofReal(e_i)=ofReal(ε/4).

argument.text: Use M020 with exponent s≥0. For each natural index i, continuity of x↦x^s at d_i and the strict gap d_i<r from F003 permit a positive η_i smaller than r−d_i and small enough that |(d_i+η_i)^s−d_i^s|<e_i. Indeed the continuity neighborhood for error e_i>0 contains an interval about d_i, and one can take half the minimum of its positive radius and r−d_i. Then d_i+η_i is in (d_i,r) and its s-power is <d_i^s+e_i. Countable choice of these individual values yields the sequence-existence statement F004; no covering sets are enlarged.

produces.statement: There exists a:ℕ→ℝ with d_i<a_i≤r and a_i^s<d_i^s+e_i for all natural i.

argument.text: Choose a from F004. By F003 and F004, 0<a_i≤r and ediam U_i=ofReal d_i≤ofReal a_i. Comparing nonnegative finite partial sums and then their suprema gives Σ_i ofReal(a_i^s)≤Σ_i ofReal(d_i^s)+Σ_i ofReal(e_i)<ofReal(ε/2)<ofReal ε. Addition of these nonnegative sums is justified by the finite partial-sum identity and taking increasing suprema; all right-hand totals here are finite. This proves the required cover and positive budgets for every r,ε under L2. Discharge L2 into the stated implication, and discharge L1 into the positive-exponent universal statement. Together with F001 this proves all the claimed cover-content and positive-budget statements. Empty cover members received positive numerical budgets in the same way; the proof also works in singleton and zero-dimensional spaces.

locals.declaration: Fix any metric space X with its Borel sigma algebra.
Fix a finite real scale δ.
Fix an arbitrary sequence V of subsets of MaxProd X.
Define ρ_i=(ediam V_i).toReal, including ρ_i=0 when V_i is empty.
Define Aproj_i as the projection of V_i to X.
Define Bproj_i as the projection of V_i to ℝ.
For each i define J_i=[inf Bproj_i,sup Bproj_i] if V_i is nonempty, and J_i=∅ otherwise.
Define W(t)_i=Aproj_i if t∈J_i and ∅ otherwise.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary X,A,s,δ and assume L1: s>0 and δ>0. Fix an arbitrary sequence V and assume L2: V covers A×I and ediam V_i≤ofReal δ for every i. Define ρ_i=(ediam V_i).toReal, Aproj_i=π_X(V_i), Bproj_i=π_ℝ(V_i). All ρ_i lie in [0,δ], and ediam V_i=ofReal ρ_i. The two coordinate projections are 1-Lipschitz, since each coordinate distance is bounded by their maximum, the source distance. Applying M021 to each projection therefore gives ediam Aproj_i≤ofReal ρ_i and ediam Bproj_i≤ofReal ρ_i. For empty V_i both projections and their diameters are empty and zero. This proves F001.

produces.statement: For every i, 0≤ρ_i≤δ, ediam V_i=ofReal ρ_i, ediam Aproj_i≤ofReal ρ_i, ediam Bproj_i≤ofReal ρ_i. Empty V_i have empty projections and ρ_i=0.

argument.text: Each Bproj_i is bounded in ℝ. If it is empty this is immediate. Otherwise, for any t_i∈Bproj_i, every t∈Bproj_i satisfies |t−t_i|≤ρ_i by F001 and the defining diameter bound. Thus Bproj_i⊆[t_i−ρ_i,t_i+ρ_i], a bounded interval. This proves the boundedness statement F002 without choosing any measurable projection or any uniform center.

produces.statement: Every real projection Bproj_i is bounded.

argument.text: Define J_i=[inf Bproj_i,sup Bproj_i] for nonempty V_i and J_i=∅ for empty V_i. For a nonempty index, M018 and F002 give Bproj_i⊆J_i, M017 gives ediam Bproj_i=ofReal(sup Bproj_i−inf Bproj_i), and M019 gives volume(J_i)=that same quantity≤ofReal ρ_i by F001. For empty indices inclusion and the zero volume bound are immediate. Every J_i is closed (or empty), hence Borel measurable; so is J_i∩I because I is closed. M019 at 0,1 also gives volume(I)=ofReal(1−0)=1. These are F003.

produces.statement: For every i, Bproj_i⊆J_i, J_i and J_i∩I are Borel measurable, and volume(J_i)≤ofReal ρ_i. Also I is Borel measurable and volume(I)=1; empty V_i give J_i=∅.

argument.text: Put c=C_s(δ,A) and W(t)_i=Aproj_i if t∈J_i, otherwise ∅. For each t∈I these sets cover A: for any x∈A, the cover V contains (x,t) in some V_i, hence x∈Aproj_i and t∈Bproj_i⊆J_i by F003. Each W(t)_i has extended diameter≤ofReal δ by F001, and its s-cost is at most ofReal(ρ_i^s)1_{J_i}(t), since s>0. N101's raw infimum formula yields c≤Σ_i ofReal(ρ_i^s)1_{J_i}(t). Define h=c1_I and g_i=ofReal(ρ_i^s)1_{J_i∩I}. On I the preceding inequality gives h≤Σ_i g_i; outside I both sides are zero. All g_i and h are Borel measurable: they take fixed constants on measurable sets and zero elsewhere, also when c=∞. This proves F004; we never require c to be finite.

produces.statement: h=c1_I and g_i=ofReal(ρ_i^s)1_{J_i∩I} are measurable nonnegative extended functions on ℝ, and h≤Σ_i g_i pointwise on ℝ.

argument.text:
Integrate the pointwise inequality of F004 with respect to volume on ℝ by M016. Apply M014 to the natural-indexed measurable family g, and M015 to h=c1_I and to each g_i. Using F003 and measure monotonicity gives
c=c·volume(I)=∫⁻h≤∫⁻Σ_i g_i=Σ_i∫⁻g_i
 =Σ_i ofReal(ρ_i^s) volume(J_i∩I)
 ≤Σ_i ofReal(ρ_i^s) volume(J_i)
 ≤Σ_i ofReal(ρ_i^s) ofReal ρ_i
 =Σ_i ofReal(ρ_i^(s+1))=Σ_i(ediam V_i)^(s+1).
For ρ_i>0 the last power identity is ρ_i^s·ρ_i=ρ_i^(s+1); for ρ_i=0 both s and s+1 are positive so both sides are zero. Empty indices also contribute zero. Measure monotonicity needs no additional measurability condition. Nonnegative sums are compared by finite partial sums and their suprema. These operations hold in [0,∞], with 0·∞=0 as usual; c·1=c even for c=∞. Since V was arbitrary, discharge L2 and universally quantify V. This is F005.

produces.statement: Every natural-indexed δ-cover V0 of A×I satisfies C_s(δ,A)≤Σ_i (ediam V0_i)^(s+1).

argument.text: Take the infimum of the cover costs in F005. N101 applies to exponent s+1>0 and gives C_s(δ,A)≤C_{s+1}(δ,A×I). This infimum argument is valid even if no δ-cover exists, in which case its right-hand infimum is ∞. The argument holds for every real δ>0. Take the supremum over these scales, and use N101 for both spaces and positive exponents s and s+1, to obtain H^s(A)≤H^{s+1}(A×I). Discharge L1 and universally quantify X,A,s,δ. This proves the slicing inequality with constant one, for arbitrary subsets and without compactness.

argument.text: Fix X,A,q, and assume L1: q>0 and H^q(A)=0. Fix arbitrary real δ,ε and assume L2: δ>0 and ε>0. Define r=min(1,δ)>0. N101, instantiated with s=q and this r,ε, gives existence of a pair consisting of a cover U of A and budgets a_i with 0<a_i≤r, ediam U_i≤ofReal a_i and Σ_i ofReal(a_i^q)<ofReal ε. Record this as F001 before choosing the pair.

produces.statement: There exist U:ℕ→Set X and a:ℕ→ℝ, chosen as one pair, such that U covers A, 0<a_i≤r, ediam U_i≤ofReal a_i, and Σ_i ofReal(a_i^q)<ofReal ε.

argument.text:
Choose the pair (U,a) from F001. Define N_i=ceil(1/a_i). Since 0<a_i≤r≤1, N_i≥1, 1/N_i≤a_i and N_i≤1/a_i+1≤2/a_i. Partition I by the N_i closed intervals Jpart_(i,j)=[j/N_i,(j+1)/N_i] for 0≤j<N_i. The products Ppart_(i,j)=U_i×Jpart_(i,j) cover A×I. Distances within each product are bounded by max(a_i,1/N_i)≤a_i, so its extended diameter is ≤ofReal a_i≤ofReal δ. Their index set {(i,j): i∈ℕ,0≤j<N_i} injects into ℕ×ℕ, which is enumerated by successive finite diagonals. Thus the products can be reindexed as a natural sequence, with empty padding if necessary. Reindexing preserves the sum of nonnegative costs: both are suprema of the same finite subfamily sums. Their total (q+1)-cost satisfies
Σ_i Σ_{j<N_i}(ediam Ppart_(i,j))^(q+1)
 ≤Σ_i ofReal(N_i a_i^(q+1))
 ≤Σ_i ofReal((2/a_i)a_i^(q+1))
 =2Σ_i ofReal(a_i^q)<ofReal(2ε).
All divisions are by positive a_i; real powers give a_i^(q+1)/a_i=a_i^q. This proves the countable-cover existence and cost bound F002, with absolute constant 2.

produces.statement: There exists a natural-indexed δ-cover of A×I in MaxProd X with total (q+1)-cost <ofReal(2ε).

argument.text: N101 identifies C_{q+1}(δ,A×I) with the cover-cost infimum. By F002 it is ≤ofReal(2ε) for every ε>0 at each fixed δ>0, so it is zero: any positive finite lower bound is contradicted by taking a smaller ε, and even one such finite bound excludes ∞. Discharge L2 to obtain the asserted existence for every δ,ε>0 and zero content for every δ>0. N101's finite-positive-scale supremum then yields H^{q+1}(A×I)=0. Discharge L1 and universally quantify X,A,q. This proves both claimed clauses, including the scale/tolerance statement and its constant.

argument.text: Fix X,A and assume L1: A is nonempty and dimH A≠∞. Define D0=(dimH A).toReal and G=A×I. Since dimH A is finite and nonnegative, D0≥0 and ofReal D0=dimH A. This establishes F001 and legitimately permits approximation by real exponents.

argument.text: Fix an arbitrary real q and assume L2: q>D0. Then q>0 by F001. Instantiate M003 with subset A and nonnegative exponent q: ofReal q>dimH A, so H^q(A)=0. N103 with X,A,q yields H^{q+1}(G)=0. Record this exact measure conclusion as F002.

Apply M004 in MaxProd X to G and exponent q+1>0, using F002's zero measure (zero≠∞). It gives dimH G≤ofReal(q+1). Since q was arbitrary, discharge L2 into the complete universally quantified assertion F003.

produces.statement: For every real q0>D0, dimH G≤ofReal(q0+1).

argument.text: Take q0=D0+1 in F003; the resulting finite upper bound proves dimH G≠∞. Define T0=(dimH G).toReal, so T0≥0 and ofReal T0=dimH G. To prove the sharp upper bound, assume L3: T0>D0+1, and define qmid=D0+(T0−D0−1)/2. Then qmid>D0 and qmid+1<T0. F003 at qmid gives T0≤qmid+1, a contradiction. Discharge L3 by classical contradiction, obtaining T0≤D0+1. Independently, N104 applies to the nonempty A from F001 and gives dimH G≥1, hence T0≥1. These finite-dimension and bound facts are F004.

produces.statement: dimH G≠∞, T0≥1, ofReal T0=dimH G, and T0≤D0+1.

argument.text: Fix an arbitrary real s and assume L4: 0<s<D0. By F001, ofReal s<dimH A. M002 at subset A and nonnegative exponent s gives H^s(A)=∞, the exact assertion F005.

produces.statement: s>0 and H^s(A)=∞.

argument.text: Instantiate N102 with X,A,s. Since s>0, F005 and its measure inequality give ∞=H^s(A)≤H^{s+1}(A×I)=H^{s+1}(G), so H^{s+1}(G)=∞. This is F006.
Apply M005 in MaxProd X at subset G and exponent s+1, using F006. It gives ofReal(s+1)≤dimH G, hence s+1≤T0 by F004. Discharge L4 and quantify the arbitrary s to obtain F007.

produces.statement: For every real s0 with 0<s0<D0, s0+1≤T0.

argument.text: By D0≥0 from F001, the cases D0=0 and D0>0 are exhaustive. In the first branch assume L5: D0=0. F004 gives T0≥1=D0+1; close this branch and discharge L5. In particular smid>0 and T0<smid+1, whereas F007 gives smid+1≤T0. This is a contradiction; discharge L7, obtaining T0≥D0+1 in this branch, and discharge L6. Case elimination therefore gives T0≥D0+1 universally. With F004's opposite bound, T0=D0+1. Since ofReal D0=dimH A and ofReal T0=dimH G, this is dimH(A×I)=dimH A+1 in [0,∞]. argument.text:
The map appendCoord(n) places the n coordinates of its first component before its real second component. Its inverse reads off these first n coordinates and the last coordinate. These coordinate operations are inverse in both orders, so the map is bijective. Fix arbitrary source points p,p′ and put a=‖p.1−p′.1‖₂≥0, b=|p.2−p′.2|≥0. Splitting the finite sum of squares into the first n terms and the last term gives
 d₂(appendCoord(n)p,appendCoord(n)p′)^2
   =Σ_{i<n}|p.1_i−p′.1_i|²+|p.2−p′.2|²=a²+b².
Since max(a,b)²≤a²+b²≤2max(a,b)², taking nonnegative square roots gives
 d_max(p,p′)≤d₂(appendCoord(n)p,appendCoord(n)p′)≤√2·d_max(p,p′).
The maximum is exactly the source distance. Quantifying p,p′, these inequalities establish √2-Lipschitz and 1-antilipschitz bounds. When n=0, the coordinate sum is empty and zero, the first component is the unique vector of Ambient 0, and the same inverse and estimates still apply. Record the full construction and bounds as F001.

Together with F001's bijectivity and the two explicit distance bounds, this proves the claimed metric bridge and dimension preservation. Both constants are absolute; no norm-invariance assertion is assumed.

original_context.full_target:
Here dimension means **Hausdorff dimension**. As approved by the user on
2026-10-23, assume explicitly that \(E\) is nonempty. With the convention
\(\dim_H\varnothing=0\), the printed equality would otherwise fail for
the empty set. This is a disclosed addition to the printed exercise.

Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove

\[
\dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
\]

The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary X,A,s, and assume L1: s>0. For an empty cover member, ediam ∅=0 and 0^s=0, so its guarded cost in Content is zero, exactly the raw diameter-power cost. For a nonempty member the supremum over its nonemptiness witnesses is that same power. Thus C_s is the stated raw countable-cover infimum. If 0<δ₁≤δ₂, each δ₁-cover is a δ₂-cover; taking infima gives C_s(δ₂,A)≤C_s(δ₁,A). Apply M001 at X,A,s. Its positive extended-scale supremum equals the positive finite real-scale supremum: every finite positive real scale is an allowed extended scale, while any h∈(0,∞] admits a finite real δ>0 with ofReal δ≤h (take δ=h.toReal/2 when h<∞, and δ=1 when h=∞). Scale antitonicity then bounds the content at h by the one at δ. This proves the normalization and supremum statements F001. The countable covers here are exactly those in problem.md; finite covers can be padded by empty sets.

produces.statement: For this X,A,s>0, C_s is the raw positive-exponent cover infimum, is antitone on positive scales, and H^s(A)=sup_{δ>0,δ∈ℝ} C_s(δ,A).

argument.text: Fix arbitrary real r,ε, and assume L2: H^s(A)=0, r>0 and ε>0. F001 and nonnegativity give C_s(r/2,A)=0. The defining infimum then has a cover with cost <ofReal(ε/4): if no admissible cover had cost below that positive number, the infimum would be at least that number. In particular admissible covers exist; otherwise the infimum is ∞. This proves F002.

produces.statement: There exists U:ℕ→Set X covering A, with ediam U_i≤ofReal(r/2) for every i and Σ_i (ediam U_i)^s<ofReal(ε/4).

argument.text: Choose U from F002, and define d_i=(ediam U_i).toReal and e_i=ε·2^(−i−3). Since ediam U_i≤ofReal(r/2)<∞, we have 0≤d_i≤r/2<r and ediam U_i=ofReal d_i. Therefore the original cost is Σ_i ofReal(d_i^s)<ofReal(ε/4). Each e_i is positive and Σ_i e_i=ε/4: the first m terms sum to (ε/4)(1−2^(−m)), tending to ε/4. These finite partial sums also establish the corresponding extended-nonnegative sum identity.

produces.statement: U covers A; 0≤d_i≤r/2<r, ediam U_i=ofReal d_i, Σ_i ofReal(d_i^s)<ofReal(ε/4), e_i>0 and Σ_i ofReal(e_i)=ofReal(ε/4).

argument.text: Use M020 with exponent s≥0. For each natural index i, continuity of x↦x^s at d_i and the strict gap d_i<r from F003 permit a positive η_i smaller than r−d_i and small enough that |(d_i+η_i)^s−d_i^s|<e_i. Indeed the continuity neighborhood for error e_i>0 contains an interval about d_i, and one can take half the minimum of its positive radius and r−d_i. Then d_i+η_i is in (d_i,r) and its s-power is <d_i^s+e_i. Countable choice of these individual values yields the sequence-existence statement F004; no covering sets are enlarged.

produces.statement: There exists a:ℕ→ℝ with d_i<a_i≤r and a_i^s<d_i^s+e_i for all natural i.

argument.text: Choose a from F004. By F003 and F004, 0<a_i≤r and ediam U_i=ofReal d_i≤ofReal a_i. Comparing nonnegative finite partial sums and then their suprema gives Σ_i ofReal(a_i^s)≤Σ_i ofReal(d_i^s)+Σ_i ofReal(e_i)<ofReal(ε/2)<ofReal ε. Addition of these nonnegative sums is justified by the finite partial-sum identity and taking increasing suprema; all right-hand totals here are finite. This proves the required cover and positive budgets for every r,ε under L2. Discharge L2 into the stated implication, and discharge L1 into the positive-exponent universal statement. Together with F001 this proves all the claimed cover-content and positive-budget statements. Empty cover members received positive numerical budgets in the same way; the proof also works in singleton and zero-dimensional spaces.

output.statement: For every metric space X, subset A⊆X, real s>0 and finite real δ>0, C_s(δ,A)≤C_{s+1}(δ,A×I) in the maximum product metric MaxProd(X). Consequently H^s(A)≤H^{s+1}(A×I), including infinite values. The slicing constant is exactly one; neither compactness nor measurability of A or its covers is required.

locals.declaration: Fix any metric space X with its Borel sigma algebra.
Fix a finite real scale δ.
Fix an arbitrary sequence V of subsets of MaxProd X.
Define ρ_i=(ediam V_i).toReal, including ρ_i=0 when V_i is empty.
Define Aproj_i as the projection of V_i to X.
Define Bproj_i as the projection of V_i to ℝ.
For each i define J_i=[inf Bproj_i,sup Bproj_i] if V_i is nonempty, and J_i=∅ otherwise.
Define W(t)_i=Aproj_i if t∈J_i and ∅ otherwise.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary X,A,s,δ and assume L1: s>0 and δ>0. Fix an arbitrary sequence V and assume L2: V covers A×I and ediam V_i≤ofReal δ for every i. Define ρ_i=(ediam V_i).toReal, Aproj_i=π_X(V_i), Bproj_i=π_ℝ(V_i). All ρ_i lie in [0,δ], and ediam V_i=ofReal ρ_i. The two coordinate projections are 1-Lipschitz, since each coordinate distance is bounded by their maximum, the source distance. Applying M021 to each projection therefore gives ediam Aproj_i≤ofReal ρ_i and ediam Bproj_i≤ofReal ρ_i. For empty V_i both projections and their diameters are empty and zero. This proves F001.

produces.statement: For every i, 0≤ρ_i≤δ, ediam V_i=ofReal ρ_i, ediam Aproj_i≤ofReal ρ_i, ediam Bproj_i≤ofReal ρ_i. Empty V_i have empty projections and ρ_i=0.

argument.text: Each Bproj_i is bounded in ℝ. If it is empty this is immediate. Otherwise, for any t_i∈Bproj_i, every t∈Bproj_i satisfies |t−t_i|≤ρ_i by F001 and the defining diameter bound. Thus Bproj_i⊆[t_i−ρ_i,t_i+ρ_i], a bounded interval. This proves the boundedness statement F002 without choosing any measurable projection or any uniform center.

produces.statement: Every real projection Bproj_i is bounded.

argument.text: Define J_i=[inf Bproj_i,sup Bproj_i] for nonempty V_i and J_i=∅ for empty V_i. For a nonempty index, M018 and F002 give Bproj_i⊆J_i, M017 gives ediam Bproj_i=ofReal(sup Bproj_i−inf Bproj_i), and M019 gives volume(J_i)=that same quantity≤ofReal ρ_i by F001. For empty indices inclusion and the zero volume bound are immediate. Every J_i is closed (or empty), hence Borel measurable; so is J_i∩I because I is closed. M019 at 0,1 also gives volume(I)=ofReal(1−0)=1. These are F003.

produces.statement: For every i, Bproj_i⊆J_i, J_i and J_i∩I are Borel measurable, and volume(J_i)≤ofReal ρ_i. Also I is Borel measurable and volume(I)=1; empty V_i give J_i=∅.

argument.text: Put c=C_s(δ,A) and W(t)_i=Aproj_i if t∈J_i, otherwise ∅. For each t∈I these sets cover A: for any x∈A, the cover V contains (x,t) in some V_i, hence x∈Aproj_i and t∈Bproj_i⊆J_i by F003. Each W(t)_i has extended diameter≤ofReal δ by F001, and its s-cost is at most ofReal(ρ_i^s)1_{J_i}(t), since s>0. N101's raw infimum formula yields c≤Σ_i ofReal(ρ_i^s)1_{J_i}(t). Define h=c1_I and g_i=ofReal(ρ_i^s)1_{J_i∩I}. On I the preceding inequality gives h≤Σ_i g_i; outside I both sides are zero. All g_i and h are Borel measurable: they take fixed constants on measurable sets and zero elsewhere, also when c=∞. This proves F004; we never require c to be finite.

produces.statement: h=c1_I and g_i=ofReal(ρ_i^s)1_{J_i∩I} are measurable nonnegative extended functions on ℝ, and h≤Σ_i g_i pointwise on ℝ.

argument.text:
Integrate the pointwise inequality of F004 with respect to volume on ℝ by M016. Apply M014 to the natural-indexed measurable family g, and M015 to h=c1_I and to each g_i. Using F003 and measure monotonicity gives
c=c·volume(I)=∫⁻h≤∫⁻Σ_i g_i=Σ_i∫⁻g_i
 =Σ_i ofReal(ρ_i^s) volume(J_i∩I)
 ≤Σ_i ofReal(ρ_i^s) volume(J_i)
 ≤Σ_i ofReal(ρ_i^s) ofReal ρ_i
 =Σ_i ofReal(ρ_i^(s+1))=Σ_i(ediam V_i)^(s+1).
For ρ_i>0 the last power identity is ρ_i^s·ρ_i=ρ_i^(s+1); for ρ_i=0 both s and s+1 are positive so both sides are zero. Empty indices also contribute zero. Measure monotonicity needs no additional measurability condition. Nonnegative sums are compared by finite partial sums and their suprema. These operations hold in [0,∞], with 0·∞=0 as usual; c·1=c even for c=∞. Since V was arbitrary, discharge L2 and universally quantify V. This is F005.

produces.statement: Every natural-indexed δ-cover V0 of A×I satisfies C_s(δ,A)≤Σ_i (ediam V0_i)^(s+1).

argument.text: Take the infimum of the cover costs in F005. N101 applies to exponent s+1>0 and gives C_s(δ,A)≤C_{s+1}(δ,A×I). This infimum argument is valid even if no δ-cover exists, in which case its right-hand infimum is ∞. The argument holds for every real δ>0. Take the supremum over these scales, and use N101 for both spaces and positive exponents s and s+1, to obtain H^s(A)≤H^{s+1}(A×I). Discharge L1 and universally quantify X,A,s,δ. This proves the slicing inequality with constant one, for arbitrary subsets and without compactness.

argument.text: Fix X,A,q, and assume L1: q>0 and H^q(A)=0. Fix arbitrary real δ,ε and assume L2: δ>0 and ε>0. Define r=min(1,δ)>0. N101, instantiated with s=q and this r,ε, gives existence of a pair consisting of a cover U of A and budgets a_i with 0<a_i≤r, ediam U_i≤ofReal a_i and Σ_i ofReal(a_i^q)<ofReal ε. Record this as F001 before choosing the pair.

produces.statement: There exist U:ℕ→Set X and a:ℕ→ℝ, chosen as one pair, such that U covers A, 0<a_i≤r, ediam U_i≤ofReal a_i, and Σ_i ofReal(a_i^q)<ofReal ε.

argument.text:
Choose the pair (U,a) from F001. Define N_i=ceil(1/a_i). Since 0<a_i≤r≤1, N_i≥1, 1/N_i≤a_i and N_i≤1/a_i+1≤2/a_i. Partition I by the N_i closed intervals Jpart_(i,j)=[j/N_i,(j+1)/N_i] for 0≤j<N_i. The products Ppart_(i,j)=U_i×Jpart_(i,j) cover A×I. Distances within each product are bounded by max(a_i,1/N_i)≤a_i, so its extended diameter is ≤ofReal a_i≤ofReal δ. Their index set {(i,j): i∈ℕ,0≤j<N_i} injects into ℕ×ℕ, which is enumerated by successive finite diagonals. Thus the products can be reindexed as a natural sequence, with empty padding if necessary. Reindexing preserves the sum of nonnegative costs: both are suprema of the same finite subfamily sums. Their total (q+1)-cost satisfies
Σ_i Σ_{j<N_i}(ediam Ppart_(i,j))^(q+1)
 ≤Σ_i ofReal(N_i a_i^(q+1))
 ≤Σ_i ofReal((2/a_i)a_i^(q+1))
 =2Σ_i ofReal(a_i^q)<ofReal(2ε).
All divisions are by positive a_i; real powers give a_i^(q+1)/a_i=a_i^q. This proves the countable-cover existence and cost bound F002, with absolute constant 2.

produces.statement: There exists a natural-indexed δ-cover of A×I in MaxProd X with total (q+1)-cost <ofReal(2ε).

argument.text: N101 identifies C_{q+1}(δ,A×I) with the cover-cost infimum. By F002 it is ≤ofReal(2ε) for every ε>0 at each fixed δ>0, so it is zero: any positive finite lower bound is contradicted by taking a smaller ε, and even one such finite bound excludes ∞. Discharge L2 to obtain the asserted existence for every δ,ε>0 and zero content for every δ>0. N101's finite-positive-scale supremum then yields H^{q+1}(A×I)=0. Discharge L1 and universally quantify X,A,q. This proves both claimed clauses, including the scale/tolerance statement and its constant.

argument.text:
The map appendCoord(n) places the n coordinates of its first component before its real second component. Its inverse reads off these first n coordinates and the last coordinate. These coordinate operations are inverse in both orders, so the map is bijective. Fix arbitrary source points p,p′ and put a=‖p.1−p′.1‖₂≥0, b=|p.2−p′.2|≥0. Splitting the finite sum of squares into the first n terms and the last term gives
 d₂(appendCoord(n)p,appendCoord(n)p′)^2
   =Σ_{i<n}|p.1_i−p′.1_i|²+|p.2−p′.2|²=a²+b².
Since max(a,b)²≤a²+b²≤2max(a,b)², taking nonnegative square roots gives
 d_max(p,p′)≤d₂(appendCoord(n)p,appendCoord(n)p′)≤√2·d_max(p,p′).
The maximum is exactly the source distance. Quantifying p,p′, these inequalities establish √2-Lipschitz and 1-antilipschitz bounds. When n=0, the coordinate sum is empty and zero, the first component is the unique vector of Ambient 0, and the same inverse and estimates still apply. Record the full construction and bounds as F001.

original_context.full_target:
Here dimension means **Hausdorff dimension**. As approved by the user on
2026-10-23, assume explicitly that \(E\) is nonempty. With the convention
\(\dim_H\varnothing=0\), the printed equality would otherwise fail for
the empty set. This is a disclosed addition to the printed exercise.

Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove

\[
\dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
\]

The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.
